content:
maya: Heads-up — after the routing-policy rollout (canary) I’m seeing a bunch of traces that start but never include any downstream DB / cache child spans, looks like trace propagation is getting lost in the path. :thinking:

sam: Which route? any sample trace id?

maya: route=api-ingest-v2, trace id `4f7c3a2e` (jaeger link: http://jaeger.internal/trace/4f7c3a2e). root + http spans exist, but no redis/postgres spans for several requests. Happened right after we enabled the `add-debug-headers` policy.

leo: I just checked exporter logs on ingest pod-3: `OTLP export failed: HTTP/2 stream reset (RST_STREAM) - reason=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` and then `dropped 12 spans`. Could be backpressure when an upstream header changed payload size.

carla: @maya can you paste the exact header set we added?

maya: We inject `x-rw-debug` with a serialized JSON of routing/debug metadata (recently added customer routing keys). Example: `x-rw-debug: {"policy":"add-debug-headers","route_state":...,"hints":...}` — some payloads can be large (~2-3KB).

sam: Ah. Envoy/sidecar has a default header size limit and some proxies strip or truncate headers > 8KB or treat long headers weirdly. But stripping traceparent would explain missing child spans. Any evidence of `traceparent` being absent?

maya: I grabbed the raw request headers from pod sidecar: `traceparent` is present on ingress but missing on the internal request to the collector. snippet: ```
# ingress-at-edge
traceparent: 00-4f7c3a2e...-01
x-rw-debug: <2.6KB JSON>
# after sidecar -> collector
x-rw-debug: <truncated>
# traceparent: <MISSING>
```

leo: That matches. Envoy treats very long header lists differently when `append_forwarded`/header buffer is full; it can drop lower-priority headers. Our sidecar config doesn't mark `traceparent` as privileged.

carla: We should avoid large debug headers. Short-term: move `x-rw-debug` into request body or compress it. Long-term: update sidecar to preserve tracing headers.

sam: Quick reproduction: `curl -v -H "traceparent: 00-4f7c3a2e-abcdef1234567890-01" -H "x-rw-debug: $(python -c 'print("x"*2500)')" http://svc/api/ingest` then dump headers captured by collector. I can repro locally, `traceparent` disappears once header size > ~2KB in our envoy config.

deploy-bot: deploy/redwood-ingest-canary started: roll 2026-06-17T15:12Z by carla

carla: I've opened PR to mark `traceparent` and `tracestate` as `preserve_tracing_headers` in the sidecar template and bump `header_buffer_size` in envoy bootstrap: https://git.internal/pr/3821 (small change). Also adding a test that sends large `x-rw-debug` and asserts traceparent forwarded.

leo: Until that ships, can we gate the policy to not add `x-rw-debug` when payload > 512 bytes? Or compress to base64 gzip and set `x-rw-debug-enc: gzip` so headers stay small.

maya: I pushed a small policy change to strip non-essential fields for now: rolled to canary in us-west only. Observability shows traces rebuilding — I can see redis/postgres child spans again for a subset. :tada:

ops-bot: metric alert resolved: exporter.drop_rate (ingest) returned to baseline at 2026-06-17T15:48Z

sam: Great. Follow-ups: 1) sidecar PR merged + release; 2) add a linter rule in routing-policy CI to warn on headers > 512 bytes; 3) add a tracing-preservation integration test in e2e.

carla: merging PR now. We'll schedule a small runtime patch for the next private cluster deploy and update the policy docs.

maya: Thanks all. Leaving tracking note: incident-telemetry-2026-06-adddebugheader in the incident board.

sam: Nice quick catch. Log of notes attached to thread. :eyes:
